editorial_note: ProofWiki Axiomatic Definition only. Its initial 'rationals plus irrationals' characterization is explicitly circular and excluded from this definition. Cauchy-class and Dedekind-cut constructions need separate source review.
text: A real-number system is a totally ordered field R in which every nonempty subset of R that is bounded above has a supremum in R. Different complete ordered-field realizations are equivalent up to an order-preserving field isomorphism.

editorial_note: ProofWiki Totally Ordered Field subsection; the article distinguishes a more general partially ordered field whose conventions vary.
text: A totally ordered field F is a field with a total order ≤ for which x<y implies x+z<y+z for every z, and x<y with z>0 implies xz<yz. Such a field is not necessarily Dedekind complete.

editorial_note: Source specifies the order-theoretic supremum property, not arbitrary metric completeness. The empty subset is expressly excluded; upper bound is taken in S.
text: An ordered set S has the Dedekind completeness property if every nonempty subset A⊆S bounded above in S has a least upper bound in S.

editorial_note: The piecewise and square-root formulations are equivalent over the reals, but the latter invokes an independently defined nonnegative square-root function. This evidence must not silently overwrite the previously screened real-absolute-value meaning.
text: For a real number x the absolute value |x| equals x if x≥0 and −x if x<0; equivalently, |x|=√(x²) where √ denotes the nonnegative real square root.
